newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond mart idles, holidays draw near.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond mart idles, holidays draw near.

text.p: The U.S. investment-grade and high-yield markets experienced a quite day on Monday as most Wall Street players had their minds on matters other than trading, according to market sources.
"Everyone (on the sell-side) is waiting for their bonuses and the buy-side is closing down their books. It feels like a pre-holiday to me," said one trader.
Traders note that many investment banks will notify their employees of their bonuses this week.
The announcement that Boeing Inc planned to acquire McDonnell Douglas Corp did spark some market excitement.
Traders bid up the price of McDonnell Douglas' senior unsecured bonds, speculating their Baa1/A- rating may be upgraded if Boeing assumes the company's debt in a merger.
Both Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service confirmed on Monday they may increase both company's ratings.

Moody's said it will assess, "the potential for improved cash flows from the combined military businesses, which should have significantly better economies of scale in a rapidly consolidating industry."
